account:
Today I have followed a full appointment schedule, but several pieces of town business seem strangely insubstantial. The mill grain inspection had no organizer identified in the appointment records. No council letters arrived for my afternoon appointment, and the account ledgers still have not been located. The secretary is investigating, but has not yet brought a definite report from the baker. I went to the bakery earlier and did not find the baker there.

There is talk of a bridge or port change at the bakery, but I have no confirmed proposal or firsthand evidence of alterations. Townsfolk 28 repeated that talk and also said the builder carried a sack of bread at market. I personally heard the baker disclaim any town charge or payment claim without evidence, and say future orders need an agreed price. That suggests some uncertainty over bread orders, but I cannot establish its connection to anything else.

My neighbour says they chatted with neighbours at the warehouse and invited them to visit. They have not named those neighbours yet, and deny seeing bridge or port alterations. The secretary has now joined us at the dockside cottage while seeking the baker. The neighbour has been welcoming and interested in whether I have time to relax, rather than offering much concrete news.

The most unusual remaining appointment is with the innkeeper at eighteen hundred in the great hall, with an explicit instruction not to arrive early. I approved it, but its purpose was not stated to the secretary. Warehouse conversations, invitations, bread being carried, and that timed meeting might fit preparations for a gathering, perhaps something meant to surprise me. That is only a suspicion, not established knowledge; I have no evidence of wrongdoing or an actual bridge or port scheme. I should keep my sixteen-thirty office appointment and then attend the innkeeper's meeting at the agreed time.
